chapter: Honors, Gibson and Dorsey late years
title: Cooking in the dressing room with Charlie Shavers
summary: After buying burners and food on 8th Avenue, Leeman and Shavers cook between shows until the aromas draw complaints and Dorsey tells them to stop.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: We were called to task on another incident. By that time, I had interested Charlie Shavers in cheifing -- because I was cheifing for him, too. He used to tell me about down home

pots and soul cooking, which he grew up on. So I used to try to please him by making spare rib stew -- that's a beauty for anybody that's interested in getting in touch with me, and Charlie said, "Well, look, let me cook this pot this time; I want to show you something."

So we went out and bought -- and this is still at the Capitol Theatre between shows -- went out and bought a double burner, an electric burner, and pots and pans, and all the food on 8th Avenue in the Italian shopping district -- this is between shows -- and I don't know, we must have spent fifty, sixty or seventy dollars at that time just getting pots and pans and the cooking utensils, and the food -- we could have eaten very nicely at any of the foremost restaurants in New York and forgotten this hobby.

But we got a one pot burner, Charlie did, and we got three pots burning between shows, and we went on and played our shows, but never realizing that the aromas were just excruciating backstage -- and the air conditioning, or the cooling system wasn't on, but the air conditioning in the hotel circulated these beautiful aromas. And Tommy came back and the manager of the hotel came back and he says, "I know you fellows like to have a good time, and I don't know what the hell you're doing, but I've had about 100,000 complaints from theatre goers here and customers about the aromas from the restaurant next door" which was filtering into the theatre - and after we finished

that pot for the band, call it a day with your cooking! That was the end of our culinary exploits for the present, and Charlie had somebody come in and build a very special crate and box so he could carry the equipment on the road with him, which he did. And he has his own kitchen from then on, and I heard many stories about his efforts as a chef.
